audit.title: VRF Security Considerations
audit.summary: This is a well-written conceptual security checklist for Chainlink VRF v2.5, and its greatest GEO strength is that most headings are already phrased as imperative directives an engine can lift verbatim ("`fulfillRandomWords` must not revert", "Don't accept bids/bets/inputs after you have made a randomness request"). Its biggest opportunity is that it is almost entirely qualitative: it repeatedly tells developers to "choose a safe block confirmation time" and "keep funded above the minimum" without a single concrete number, code example, or external reference (ERC-4337 is named but not linked). Combined with absent metadata (no JSON-LD, canonical, or dates), the page is retrievable and quotable for *what to do* but weak on *the specifics agents need to act*. Honest verdict: strong bones, under-specified body — Developing.

recommendations.title: Replace vague quantities with concrete figures
recommendations.where: "Choose a safe block confirmation time…" and "Keep your subscription funded well above the minimum balance"
recommendations.issue: "choose an appropriate confirmation time" / "well above the minimum balance"
recommendations.change: State the actual configurable range (e.g. "`requestConfirmations` accepts 3–200 blocks; defaults and recommended values vary by chain — see the [Supported Networks](/vrf/v2-5/supported-networks) table") and give a concrete funding heuristic (e.g. "fund to at least Nx the per-request max cost").
recommendations.why: Quantitative claims with units are among the highest-lift retrieval signals; qualitative-only prose underperforms and cannot be acted on by agents.

recommendations.title: Add a per-chain confirmation-time table
recommendations.where: "Choose a safe block confirmation time, which will vary between blockchains"
recommendations.issue: section asserts values "vary between blockchains" but shows none
recommendations.change: Insert a small table (chain · min confirmations · recommended for high-value apps) or link directly to the network table with the specific column.
recommendations.why: Tables let engines extract reasons and specific values per entity; this directly answers "how many confirmations for VRF on <chain>".

recommendations.title: Add short code snippets for the two code-adjacent directives
recommendations.issue: patterns described in prose only; 0 fenced blocks (measured)
recommendations.change: Add a labeled ```solidity``` block showing a `mapping(uint256 => ...)` requestId→request store and a minimal `contract X is VRFConsumerBaseV2Plus` skeleton with imports.
recommendations.why: Complete, copy-pasteable snippets are what coding agents lift; prose descriptions of code are not runnable.

recommendations.title: Add inline authoritative links
recommendations.change: Link "ERC-4337" to the EIP (`https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-4337`) and link `VRFConsumerBaseV2Plus`/`VRFCoordinatorV2_5` to their API reference pages.
recommendations.why: Inline links to primary sources raise credibility and citation rate; the page currently has 0 external references (measured).

recommendations.title: Emit page metadata
recommendations.change: Add `TechArticle` JSON-LD with `dateModified`, a canonical URL, and `inLanguage`. Surface a visible "Last updated" line.
recommendations.why: Freshness and schema are E-E-A-T signals engines use to trust and rank security guidance.

recommendations.title: Add a symptom-phrased troubleshooting subsection
recommendations.issue: no error-string or "why is my fulfillment delayed" framing
recommendations.change: Add H2s like "Why did my VRF fulfillment never arrive?" (points to reverting `fulfillRandomWords` and low balance) and "Why are my fulfillments delayed?" (concurrent consumers near minimum balance).
recommendations.why: Devs/agents query by symptom, not concept; symptom headings win retrieval that directive-titled prose misses.

antiPatterns: Vague quantifiers flagged by measurement: "many, some, significant" — plus "some time", "appropriate", "well above". Replace with concrete values (see P1).
No dated/freshness signal on a security page — mild staleness risk for time-sensitive guidance.
Two sections describe code patterns without providing code.
offPageNotes: JSON-LD, canonical URL, and last-updated signals are likely controlled by the site template — fix once at the layout level to benefit all VRF pages.
`llms.txt` is already referenced at the top of the page (good); ensure this security page is enumerated in it.
Raw `<head>` was not captured — the CLI should pass it so metadata can be fully verified rather than inferred from the served HTML.
